name: Draco
text: [approach] Reach the south face by taking the Bugaboo Glacier west, passing below the south face of Snowpatch Spire.

name: Toilet Seat
grade: 5.15d V-easy WI8 M16+ A0 Steep Snow

name: West Ridge
text: [approach] From the Conrad Kain hut and Applebee campground, go up to the Bugaboo-Snowpatch col, then cross the Upper Vowell Glacier heading west to the foot of Pigeon Spire.
[approach] Continue north past the spire to the highest point of the glacier then scramble up to the ridge crest from the south side, where the route begins.
[approach] Expect glacier travel with crevasses and snow bridges, so carry rope and glacier gear.
[descent_text] At the low point of the ridge, descend the glacier and return over the Bugaboo-Snowpatch col to the hut.

name: Stonecrop Face
text: [overview] The exact line depends on season and snow cover;
[overview] the ice tends to be at its finest around midsummer once spring snow has gone, though ice that is exposed in late season makes the climbing more engaging.
[detailed_rack] Pickets and screws;
[approach] Take the Joffre Lakes trail to the upper lake, where parties often camp below the face, then continue up the Stonecrop Glacier.

name: Lee/Hinkkala North West Face Route - Rugged Mountain
text: [overview] The lower third is moderate hard snow with small ice patches and some outcrops of rock, leading to a chimney with good ice and a grade 3 exit.

[overview] About 4-5 long pitches reach a rightward-trending ramp, followed by steep snice pitches with a rock alcove belay, a steep snow ramp, and a brief gully with exposure before steep snow to the summit.
[overview] Descend by a v-thread rappel, the East ridge, and three 60 m rappels to the glacier.
[detailed_rack] Rack used: 2 pickets, 1 fluke or deadman, 7 screws (2 x 13, 4 x 16, 1 x 22), cams .3 to #2, 6 nuts, 6 pins, bird beak, bulldog, 2 tricams, plus 7 alpine quickdraws and 4 screamers.

name: South Ridge
text: [overview] Leave Sunny Knob uphill, working through low 5th-class ground and snowfields for about 3,000 vertical feet to Phantom Tower's base.
[overview] Next take the snowfield rightward to a smaller notch, then the rock buttress to the crest, where pitches reach 5.9.
[overview] Descend that notch's far side by rappelling an icy, snowy gully down to Upper Tellot Glacier.
[detailed_rack] Medium rock rack with bail gear for the rappels, and maybe a picket or two.
[approach] low fifth class between snowfields leads to the base of Phantom Tower.
[descent_text] From the notch below the summit block, rappel down the icy, snowy gully behind the notch on the northeast side to the Upper Tellot Glacier, then cross the glacier to the Plummer Hut.

name: East Ridge
text: [overview] Very steep ridge, rated R, of decomposed marble whose granulation resembles BBs or corn snow;
[approach] The route begins from Cairn Cabin by climbing the glacier to the Footstool, the feature at the foot of the steep east ridge.

name: East Pillar of Labor Day Horn (Neufeld/Brayshaw)
text: [overview] A snow ramp running diagonally alongside the north buttress leads to the gap behind the conspicuous gendarme.
[approach] Follow the Slesse Memorial Trail to the Propeller Cairn, then traverse south across snowpatches to the Labour Day Horn buttress.
[approach] A long diagonal snow ramp runs beside the north buttress up to a notch behind the prominent gendarme, which is the start of the pillar.

name: Flight 810 Buttress
text: [descent_text] Depending on the snow, the couloir can be a continuous downclimb on snow or a series of rappels over polished rock with weak anchors.
[descent_text] Downclimbing snow is the safer choice when conditions allow.

name: North East  Headwall Variation
text: [approach] Continue north over glacier-polished slabs, losing a little height toward a wooded ridge, and scramble a short gully (third to fourth class, often damp) to a notch in it.
[approach] Drop into the cirque below the pocket glacier and climb slabs toward the head of the bowl, where the diagonal bypass ledge begins the Northeast Buttress.
[approach] Ice can fall onto these slabs from the glacier above, so cross the exposed stretch without stopping.
[descent_text] A cairn marks where the route leaves that trail for a notch, then crosses steep snow (an ice axe is useful) and contours around Mount Parkes to Crossover Pass.

name: North Pillar
text: [descent_text] A cairn marks where the route leaves that trail for a notch, then crosses steep snow (an ice axe is useful) and contours around Mount Parkes to Crossover Pass.

name: North Rib (Kiesel/Lowe)
text: [detailed_rack] Bring a full rack, and an axe and crampons for the approach.
[descent_text] A cairn marks where the route leaves that trail for a notch, then crosses steep snow (an ice axe is useful) and contours around Mount Parkes to Crossover Pass.

name: Northeast Buttress
text: [what_to_bring] ice axe — if snow.
[what_to_bring] light crampons or microspikes — if snow

[approach] Ice can fall onto these slabs from the glacier above, so cross the exposed stretch without stopping.
[descent_text] A cairn marks where the route leaves that trail for a notch, steep snowfields (bring an axe or at least crampons) and a contour around Mount Parkes to Crossover Pass.

name: Russian Roulette
text: [descent_text] A cairn marks where the route leaves that trail for a notch, then crosses steep snow (an ice axe is useful) and contours around Mount Parkes to Crossover Pass.

text: [overview] Mostly rock, with possibly some easy snow.
[descent_text] A cairn marks where the route leaves that trail for a notch, then crosses steep snow (an ice axe is useful) and contours around Mount Parkes to Crossover Pass.

name: Becky/Mather (Free) 5.12- (or 5.11+ C1 for 4m)
text: [approach] The route starts at the far left (south) side of the east face: look for the big pillar shaped like an elephant trunk and start to its right, up a short finger crack from the glacier.
[approach] descend to the glacier below the wall and walk to the base, stepping across the moat at the rock, which gets harder as summer goes on.
[approach] Bring an axe and rope for the glacier.

name: Buckingham Route (easy version)
text: [overview] It sits on the north end of Snowpatch's west face, faces northwest and can be cold.
[approach] Cross the glacier to the Bugaboo-Snowpatch col;
[approach] rope up for crevasses and carry an ice axe and crampons, which can stay at the base.

name: Furry Pink Arete
text: [approach] The west face is reached by crossing the glacier to the Bugaboo-Snowpatch col;
[approach] rope up for crevasses and carry an ice axe and crampons, which can stay at the base.
[approach] From the col a snow slope leads along the foot of the face to the start.
[descent_text] Rappel that line on its bolted and chained anchors and finish via the Bugaboo-Snowpatch col or the Pigeon-Snowpatch rappels.

name: Minotaur Direct
text: [overview] An easier, direct take on Minotaur up the east face of Snowpatch, 16 pitches following old aid lines and fresh ground, notably the first four pitches through the big scar of bare rock.
[overview] A 60 m rap from the top of P4 reaches the top of P2, and a second rap reaches the snow.
[approach] The route climbs the east face: locate the obvious scoop in the large rock scar and start off the snow in the cracks on the left side of it.
[approach] descend to the glacier below the wall and walk to the base, stepping across the moat at the rock, which gets harder as summer goes on.
[approach] Bring an axe and rope for the glacier.

name: Sendero Norte
text: [approach] The route climbs the centre of the east face: descend to the glacier below the wall and walk to the base, stepping across the moat at the rock, which gets harder as summer goes on.
[approach] Bring an axe and rope for the glacier.

name: Snowpatch Route (aka SE Corner/Wiessner's Route)
text: [approach] From the hut area continue up onto the Pigeon arm of the Bugaboo Glacier.
[approach] Pass the steep rock of the southeast spur, then cross snow to a col in the spur, where the roped climbing begins.
[approach] Rope up for crevasses and carry an axe and crampons.

[descent_text] Afterward walk north to the Bugaboo-Snowpatch col and rappel or downclimb its snow, or head south to the Pigeon-Snowpatch rappels, which end on the Bugaboo Glacier and are a longer way back.
[descent_text] Rope up for the crevasses on either glacier.

name: Southwest Ridge - Direct Finish
text: [approach] The face is reached by crossing the glacier to the Bugaboo-Snowpatch col;
[approach] rope up for crevasses and carry an ice axe and crampons, which can stay at the base.
[approach] From the col a snow slope leads along the foot of the face to the start.
[descent_text] Descend by the Kraus-McCarthy rappels on bolted and chained anchors, then choose the Bugaboo-Snowpatch col, which is much faster back to Applebee, or the Pigeon-Snowpatch rappels.
[descent_text] If the final slabs hold snow, a tricky variation west of the wet area avoids them.
[descent_text] Swap wet rock shoes for approach shoes at the bottom if snow remains.

name: Sunshine Crack
text: [approach] Carry an axe and crampons, and rope up for the glacier.

name: Surfs Up
text: [approach] Surfs Up is at the south end of the west face, just left of the Pigeon icefall rappel line.
[approach] The west face is reached by crossing the glacier to the Bugaboo-Snowpatch col;
[approach] rope up for crevasses and carry an ice axe and crampons, which can stay at the base.
[approach] From the col a snow slope leads along the foot of the face to the start.

name: Welcome to the Machine
text: [approach] descend to the glacier below the wall and walk to the base, stepping across the moat at the rock, which gets harder as summer goes on.
[approach] Bring an axe and rope for the glacier.

name: Wildflowers
text: [approach] The west face is reached by crossing the glacier to the Bugaboo-Snowpatch col;
[approach] rope up for crevasses and carry an ice axe and crampons, which can stay at the base.
[approach] From the col a snow slope leads along the foot of the face to the start.
[descent_text] At the bottom continue to the Bugaboo-Snowpatch col or the Pigeon-Snowpatch rappels.

name: Beckey-Chouinard
text: [overview] confirm ropes reach the glacier below the bergschrund before committing.
[approach] From the Applebee or Kain Hut area, climb to the Bugaboo-Snowpatch Col and walk west over the upper Vowell Glacier, aiming for the crest of it beside Pigeon Spire on the north.

[approach] Drop into the Pigeon-Howser Col, scramble down large boulders onto a steep loose slope, then go down the glacier beyond, skirting big crevasses and curving north toward the East Creek bivy site, which looks straight at the tower.

[descent_text] The first group follows the north ridge toward Central Howser Tower, and the later ones angle toward the east ridge, down a gully, a steep northeast-facing buttress and short steps to the anchor above the bergschrund.
[descent_text] A final rappel over the bergschrund lands on the Vowell Glacier, where low-angle snow allows walking off.
[descent_text] Walk back across the glacier to the Applebee side.

name: It's pronounced Cleavest
text: [overview] Reach a ridge with sparse trees, cross three rock steps, and join easier snow slopes beneath the crest.

name: Whatever's Clever
text: [overview] Head up the broad scree basin into the upper couloir, then ice reaching 65 degrees and snow reaching 70 degrees lead to a sub-summit.

name: Northeast Buttress (Up In Smoke)
text: [overview] The lower buttress takes roughly 16 to 18 pitches of rock at mid-5th standard (up to 5.7) on the crest's left side, ending at the mid-height snowpatch.
[overview] Three pitches climb the lowest ice arete, which is low-angle and likely just snow early in the season;

name: Tantalus Standard Route
text: [detailed_rack] Standard alpine rack: a screw or two, possibly a picket for the bergshrund, long slings and a complete set of cams.
[approach] The route is reached by crossing the Dione Glacier below the peak.
[approach] Expect a bergschrund at the base of the climb, where a screw or a picket helps.

name: Sentinel Direct
text: [overview] Cornices form over gullies on the ridgeline, so avoid shortcuts across early-season snow.
[approach] Drop onto snow and talus to reach the foot of the northeast face.
[descent_text] cornices build over the gullies beside it, so avoid cutting across snow early in the season.

name: The Heretic
text: [overview] cornices form over the gullies, so avoid shortcuts across early-season snow.

name: Reinhold Pussycat
text: [approach] Reach the East Creek basin by climbing the Bugaboo Snowpatch Col to the upper Vowell Glacier, crossing toward the Pigeon-Howser Col and descending to the East Creek Glacier.
[approach] Climb the snow to the first weakness left of the major gash that splits the southwest face;
[approach] depending on snow level, step across the gap to a sloping ledge to rope up on, or climb a few meters from a crack on the right.

name: Complete Northwest Ridge
text: [approach] From Settler Creek, walk the logging road up to its switchback beneath the headwall under Settler Lake, ford the creek, bushwhack to snow and scree, and climb the big couloir to the col.

name: East Buttress of the South Peak
text: [what_to_bring] stiff boots — to kick steps in the permanent snow on the approach
[approach] Above Daiphy Lake, climb talus to the col on the south side of the peak, then cross the broad snowfield to its southeast and contour down to the east buttress.

name: North Ridge
text: [approach] Reach it over the Sphinx Glacier by the Castle Towers approach, or paddle the lake to Sphinx Bay and climb from there.
[approach] Then go up the glacier to the foot of the north ridge.

name: Archduke Trio
text: [overview] Three rappels down the ridgeline reach the glacier.
[approach] Start on the lower Vowell Glacier, work up into the cirque, and bear right to the beginning of the route.
[descent_text] From the third summit, rappel the ridgeline down to the glacier.

name: Northeast Arete
text: [overview] Starting at Wedgemount Hut, get onto the glacier and bear left to the col between Wedge and Weart.
[detailed_rack] Glacier travel gear and pickets;

name: Beckey route/Speedway
text: [descent_text] Once on top, the usual way off is the east-side walk-off: head for the saddle between the true summit and the false summit, where a snow patch often lingers into summer, then follow the trail down through the meadow bowl behind the peak.
